reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs with no counterparty comment — exactly what is expected for a compliant finding.

The cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right against the Customer; §1 imposes only cooperation/access for service delivery and §5 creates no examination right, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain.

Absence of any Vendor audit right is at least as favourable to us as the preferred position, so treating it as compliant (rather than 'missing', which would perversely require inserting an obligation against ourselves) is the correct classification, and no redline is warranted.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is expected noise where no audit clause exists and does not undercut the substance.
The rationale's side note on Kubient-measured impressions and the lack of an AP-side verification right is correctly parked for a reporting/revenue-verification rule rather than double-flagged here.
